newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower but spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds lower but spreads tighten.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were slightly lower in late trading on Wednesday but yield spreads on pass-throughs tightened to comparable Treasuries, dealers said.
"Mortgages have put in a very good performance today," a pass-through trader said.
The steeper Treasury yield curve helps out mortgages by aiding the collateralized mortgage obligation arbitrage, the trader said. "I think that contributed to the strength in mortgages."
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent pass-throughs were off 6/32 at 99-5/32 to yield 102 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae paper was also down 6/32 at 99-5/32, and Freddie Mac 7.5s were 6/32 lower at 99-10/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was 12/32 weaker at 99-8/32 to yield 6.73 percent.
As for secondary market activity, another trader noted that a large account purchased conventional 8.0 percent pass-throughs.
